newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian Metals - Markets quiet as contracts negotiated.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals - Markets quiet as contracts negotiated.

text.p: Asia's metals markets were quiet on Monday with the long-term supply contract negotiation and renewal season in full swing, metals traders said.
"Everyone is out campaigning for long-term contracts," said a senior metals trader based in Hong Kong, noting that the season would last another three to five weeks.
A major Chinese state-run trading firm was heard placing less copper in Thailand than in the previous contract, but this could not be confirmed.
China's domestic copper market was weak as shipments bought in June and July at around $2,000 per tonne CIF Shanghai, were arriving around this time, a Chinese metals trader at a state-run firm said.
"There is about 50,000 tonnes of copper arriving at around this time, putting pressure on prices," he said.
Most of the Chinese buyers had bought at a fixed price and had already sold on the Shanghai Metal Exchange, the metals trader said.
Metals traders reported Chinese original material or re-sold copper from the LME being offered in the market, but noted that prices were too high to be attractive.
Other metals traders said there was plenty of zinc and lead available on the market but there were no takers as customers were negotiating long-term contracts.

"The Chinese are offering LME plus $40-50 per tonne, FOB China, for 99.99 percent zinc, and special high-grade zinc (99.995 percent purity), was about $50-60 per tonne, FOB China," one zinc source said, noting that fixed asset costs rather than LME swings were of paramount concern.
